content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I’m using a [product_name] [article_no] with [product_name] [version_no] for controlling a water cooling system. It worked flawlessly for two weeks, but recently, the [product_name] [version_no] stopped displaying message texts from the program. My first thought was that it might have exited RUN mode, but upon checking, I saw the base module was still executing its logic, as outputs were reacting to changing inputs. Further investigation revealed the [product_name] [version_no] couldn't communicate with the base module anymore. I directly connected my laptop to the base module using a crossover cable and performed a port scan, suspecting it might have reverted to an old IP address. However, I couldn't find any IP address through IPCONFIG, and netstat -r didn’t show any address either. It seems like the base module’s ethernet port has stopped working. Is there a factory reset procedure to restart the base module and restore connection to the [product_name] [version_no] for another attempt?

Hi, changing IP settings won’t resolve this directly. Please check these points: - Verify the base module’s IP address is correct. - Confirm the [product_name] [version_no] IP address is correct. - Ensure the intended base module IP in the [product_name] [version_no] settings is set properly. You can connect your PC via ethernet cable to the base module, open Command Prompt (search 'CMD' in Windows), and use: ping <base module IP> You should get four reply lines from <base module IP>. Repeat this for the [product_name] [version_no] IP address. If the reply times out, the device cannot be reached at that IP. Has anyone possibly changed IPs for the base module or [product_name] [version_no]? If you suspect this, check the cabinet. Attached is an image showing how the Command Prompt should look.

Hi, I already tried every possible way to determine the base module’s IP address with Microsoft utilities, just in case the module had switched networks, but none of the ping or configuration commands like IPCONFIG /all, ARP -a, netstat -a, mdstat, etc. identified it. I installed "Wireshark" to detect all traffic over the ethernet, hoping to see the IP address and reconfigure the network, but direct connection via regular or crossover cables produced no results. The method was verified by connecting to the [product_name] [version_no], where its IP and MAC address were detected, along with some hardware descriptions not available from Microsoft tools. I’m sure now that my base module’s ethernet port has shut down. Since my [article_no] came with a [product_name] [version_no], and the base module has no external display or buttons, I’ve lost all means to interact with it. Is there a factory reset available to revert the IP to default and restore ethernet functionality, so I can reconnect both [product_name] [version_no] and my laptop to start over?
If the base module has a display, you can view the IP address in the system menu.
Hello everyone, just trying to help - is there a method to prepare a program on an SD card that loads an IP address and a blank application into the affected base module?

Hello everyone, the [article_no] supports direct cable connection, but the [article_no] only has Ethernet. If the Ethernet port disables itself, there's no way to communicate with the base module. It's essentially inaccessible at that point.

Hi [user_name], I haven’t attempted using an SD card yet, but I assume Ethernet connectivity is needed to instruct the base module to switch from internal memory and execute the program from the SD card.

analysis.insight_summary: The main issue involves a loss of connectivity between a [product_name] base module and its operator device, traced to the base module’s ethernet port unexpectedly disabling itself, making it unreachable via standard Windows networking tools and both regular and crossover cables. Attempts to scan or detect the IP address using third-party utilities were unsuccessful. The absence of a display or physical controls on this version means the user cannot access network settings or perform troubleshooting locally. Unless a factory reset option is available, the user cannot restore network access or reconfigure the device.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is hoping to regain access to the base module—preferably through a reset procedure that restores default network settings and functionality—so they can reconnect their operator device and laptop, re-establishing system configuration and communication.
